title: The Printing Press and the Reformation

cards.h: One man's list of complaints went viral in 1517
cards.b:
On 31 October 1517, a German monk named Martin Luther sent 95 arguments against the sale of indulgences to church leaders. Tradition says he nailed them to a church door in Wittenberg. Historians are unsure.

Within weeks, printers had copied it across Germany. Without the press, it might have been forgotten.

Johannes Gutenberg, a goldsmith in Mainz, built a printing press with movable metal type around 1450. The Gutenberg Bible appeared around 1455. About 180 copies were printed, and 49 survive in whole or part.

By 1500, Europe had printed perhaps 20 million volumes in presses in over 200 towns. Books became cheaper than manuscripts.
An indulgence was a church document that reduced punishment for sins. Luther's attack on its sale was the spark.

At the Diet of Worms (1521), Emperor Charles V ordered Luther to take back his writings. Luther refused. The line 'Here I stand, I can do no other' is attached to him, but many historians think it was added later.

A friendly prince, Frederick of Saxony, hid him in Wartburg Castle. There Luther translated the New Testament into German (1522).

Other reformers emerged. Zwingli in Zurich, and John Calvin in Geneva, whose ideas shaped Presbyterian and Reformed churches. In England, Henry VIII broke from Rome in 1534 (the Act of Supremacy) mostly because he wanted an heir and a new marriage.

The Catholic Church answered with the Counter-Reformation and the Jesuits (founded 1540).

Fighting broke out. The Peace of Augsburg (1555) let each German prince choose Catholic or Lutheran for his lands. Later came the Thirty Years' War (1618-1648), which killed millions, especially in Germany.

It ended with the Peace of Westphalia, often linked to the idea of sovereign states.

Myth: yes.Fact: China had woodblock printing by the 8th century and movable type by about 1040. Korea printed a Buddhist book with metal type, the Jikji, in 1377. Gutenberg's real contribution was a practical system for Europe: an adjustable mould, a press, and oil-based ink.

Also, Luther did not intend to split the Church at first.

The first printing press in Asia

In 1556 Jesuits brought a printing press to Goa, the first in Asia, and the first book came off it in 1557. In 1563 Garcia da Orta printed his Colloquies on the drugs and plants of India there.

In 1578 a press at Quilon printed a Tamil prayer book, among the first books ever printed in an Indian script. Akbar saw printed books from the Jesuits but his court kept to hand-copied manuscripts and painters.

Printing spread slowly. William Carey's Serampore press, set up in 1800, printed the Bible and grammars in dozens of Indian languages. Newspapers came with it and became a tool of the later reform and freedom movements.

Five things to remember

  1. Gutenberg's press (c. 1450) cut the cost of books.
  2. Luther's 95 Theses (1517) spread by print.
  3. Protestant movements and the Counter-Reformation split Europe.
  4. The Thirty Years' War ended in 1648.
  5. India's first printing came in Goa, 1556.

Think about it

  • What would Luther have achieved without print?
  • What is today's printing press?
